reasons: Claimed status is compliant, and the cited text supports it: § 3 (p0029, p0035, p0039) contains only substantive use restrictions with no verification, records, reporting or access mechanism, and § 20 (p0134) is a general-matters heading with no inspection right.

Absence of any audit/inspection right running against the Customer is strictly more favourable than the preferred position (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor cost, no system access), so no redline is the correct minimal edit; no comment is expected for a compliant finding.

The failing 'audit frequency limited' deterministic check is a false signal here — frequency-capping language can only exist alongside an audit clause, and inserting it would manufacture a counterparty audit right, contrary to the rule's intent.

Rationale correctly distinguishes the near-hits (escrow examination/testing right in our favour at p0114; one-time post-termination cessation certification at p0118) from a recurring audit or system-access right, and appropriately notes the preferred parameters should be inserted if Vendor later proposes a verification/usage-reporting clause.
